key_insight: A hybrid ROM-plus-neural-operator framework can learn CFD-level transient flow in an SMR helical coil steam generator, with different models excelling at either instantaneous vortical dynamics or mean-flow prediction.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster surrogate simulations for digital twins of small modular reactors, supporting real-time thermal-hydraulic monitoring and design decisions without full CFD cost.
method: MLP autoencoder + DeepONet for unstructured-mesh CFD data (L-DeepONet)
Convolutional autoencoder + DeepONet for structured-mesh CFD data
Multi-scale augmentation and FNO variants to reduce spectral bias and compare performance
evidence_signal: According to the abstract, the multi-scale L-DeepONet captured periodic Kármán vortex streets in velocity and pressure, while FNO variants produced reliable mean-flow and pressure-drop predictions.
watch_item: Model choice is task-dependent: high-resolution transient vortices and averaged flow quantities are not equally well served by the same surrogate, so deployment needs careful validation for the target DT objective.
paper_title: Neural Operator-Based Surrogate Model for CFD:Helical Coil Steam Generator in Small Modular Reactor
